_comment: A KEYM v2 container written with PBKDF2 at 1,000 iterations — far below the
600,000 this version enforces on encryption. It stands in for a backup made
It cannot be produced by the app or by reference/keym2.py: both refuse to
WRITE below the floor. Both still READ it, which is the point — §6's bounds
are write-side by design, because a backup tool that declines to open old
files has failed at the one job it exists for.
Frozen here rather than generated at test time so the fixture cannot drift
with the writer, and so the suite needs no Python.
plaintext: an old backup, made before the floor existed
writtenBy: reference/keym2.py with check_write_policy() disabled in a throwaway copy
verifiedBy: the unmodified reference/keym2.py decrypts it and reports iterations=1000
